annotation.title_clean: Towards Trustworthy Physical Intelligence: From Theory to Practice Across the Life Cycle
annotation.title_en: Towards Trustworthy Physical Intelligence: From Theory to Practice Across the Life Cycle
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Yang, W.; Liu, H.; Xu, X.; Menon, A.; Cai, X.; He, Y.; et al.
annotation.summary_en: An arXiv survey preprint arguing that existing trustworthy AI frameworks miss challenges specific to physical intelligence, such as physical safety, cyber-physical security and manufacturing. It traces the physical AI life cycle across five stages. It proposes two frameworks: T-PAIO, for putting governance into practice at each stage, and T-PAI, a set of trustworthiness principles for physical AI.
key_provisions_or_claims: Digital-centric trustworthy AI frameworks do not capture the irreversible physical consequences of physical intelligence.
Failures in physical AI spread from earlier to later stages of the life cycle, as incidents with humanoid robots and robotaxis show.
T-PAIO puts governance into practice across research, design, data, model and deployment, using quantitative checks such as lineage completeness.
The T-PAI framework covers five areas: robust and safe operation; human-centred values; integrity, privacy and equity; accountability and oversight; and sustainability.
Traceability and explainability of robot policies and data provenance are essential for accountability.
